decisions.decision: Independent and joint elicitation are two readings of two instruments, and neither is the other's correction. Asked question-by-question in bcde-validation-1, the reviewer's own answers contradict the gate table on 9 occasions across 8 of 20 answered artworks = 45%. Re-asked jointly, with the gate and its dependent on screen together, in bcde-gate-reconciliation-1, 0 contradictions remain = 0%. The 45% figure is NOT a reviewer defect and the comparison against the pre-registered <=10% ceiling is a category error. The ceiling was registered in PREMISE_NEXT.md §15.6-(3) FOR THE MODEL, whose constrained decode generates the gate first and the dependent in the gate's context, so its coherence is structurally forced: the model's low contradiction rate is architecture, not virtue, and it does not transfer to a human answering each question in isolation — least of all under an instruction that expressly forbade making the answers cohere. The reviewer's own account, 2026-08-03: "on some artworks if you ask me "is there a subject?" i might answer "no", but if you ask me *separately* "what is the subject?" i would answer "an animal". So if you ask me to *not make a story* then I will give you those 2 answers, but if you ask me *jointly* (or just one after the other) then I will change my answers so they are coherent together." On that account the independent pair carries MORE information than the reconciled one: has_dominant_subject = none with subject_kind = animal decodes as 'nothing dominates, but an animal is present', and the joint format cannot express that at all — forcing coherence collapses two variables onto one and the second is lost. The operating rule that follows: every figure must be labelled with its elicitation mode and the two must never be blended. A downstream consumer of the labels reads the STANDING (joint) state, because it must read exactly one and supersession picks it by recency, not by correctness. Any statement about what the reviewer perceives, or about how by-question elicitation behaves, reads the INDEPENDENT state. What the 45% actually measures is how often the gate's variable (does a dominant X exist) and its dependent's variable (what kind is the best-available X) come apart on real covers.

decisions.decision: The census-aware re-score is NOT cosmetic, and it changes NO conclusion. Counting a known near-duplicate of the query as a hit moves R@1 by 16-18 points (dinov2-vitl14 0.789 -> 0.952), because a same-artwork pair usually sits above cosine 0.95 and so does almost anything that outranks it — which is the census's own threshold. Standing readings: (a) STRICT R@1 is a lower bound on usefulness and an unbiased estimate of same-artwork identity; CENSUS-AWARE R@1 is an upper bound on usefulness and an overestimate of identity; the truth for any use lies between them and the gap does not matter to the decision. (b) THE ARM ORDER IS UNCHANGED under strict_intersection, the only standard symmetric across the arms that wrote it; the one nominal flip under the union (pe-core edging dinov2) is an artifact of pe-core contributing 1,333 census pairs to dinov2's 566 and vanishes under the symmetric standard. (c) THE dinov2-vs-dinov3 SEPARATION STRENGTHENS, not weakens (p = 1.4e-22 strict -> 1.2e-34 union edge, 6.7e-38 intersection). (d) THE dinov2-vs-pe-core PAIR REMAINS UNSEPARATED, and what separates them is still the reviewer's artist-leakage observation alone; this re-score adds no evidence there and does not weaken it. (e) REFEREE STANDARDS MEASURE ARCHITECTURAL KINSHIP, NOT QUALITY, and must never be quoted as verdicts on a cross-family pair: the two referees disagree violently on dinov2-vs-pe-core, both at p < 1e-25, and dinov3-vitl16 agrees with dinov2 on 78.8% of its census edges against pe-core's 65.8%. No census standard is genuinely neutral; strict_intersection is the least-bad and is still not neutral.

fundingCaveats: A CENSUS HIT IS NOT THE SAME ARTWORK. The census joins files with different artwork ids at cosine >= 0.95 across three arms; a pair may be one photograph under two catalogue entries, a reissue, a colour-graded variant, or two covers that genuinely look alike. Census-aware R@1 is therefore NOT an estimate of 'how often the model finds another rendition of the same cover' — the strict number is the only one that answers that.

decisions.decision: THE METRIC FOLLOWS THE PAIR. Reviewer ruling, 2026-08-04, verbatim: "the contrast limit between foreground and background/surface/gradient, and between accent and background/surface/gradient should be about APCA contrast, not APCA *and* color distance. Color distance is used between background and surface, or between foreground and accent." And, the same day, refining what that means for the accent, verbatim: "yes, we want to keep that class of accents [isoluminant], but then the color distance must be something else than the bracketing calibration tests we've been running. Because if APCA says 0 (or close to it) and then we use 'minimal OKLab distance at which I can see the difference' those accents will still be hardly perceptible (could *sometimes* be fine for accents, will not be fine at all for foreground)." SO THE ASSIGNMENT IS: foreground vs background/surface/rendered ramp — raw APCA ALONE, no escape at any distance and at any floor level. Accent vs background/surface/rendered ramp — raw APCA with ONE escape, and the escape runs on a FUNCTIONAL distance rather than a detection one. Background vs surface — OKLab distance at the regional same-colour bar, unchanged. Foreground vs accent — OKLab distance at an elevated bar, which is where the retired detection threshold RELOCATES, as the ruling directs. THE CHANGE IS NOT 'DROP THE ACCENT'S SECOND DIMENSION' BUT 'THE SECOND DIMENSION WAS MEASURED AGAINST THE WRONG CRITERION': the old escape ran on a DETECTION criterion ("can you see the difference"), and the reviewer ruled detection the wrong instrument for a contrast escape. MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, WHICH THE REVIEWER ASKED TO BE TOLD ABOUT: over the 554 real reviewer-verdicted palettes in data/legacy, the roles matrix newly fails 3 — TWO OF THEM ENDORSEMENTS (one I3.foreground-accent-not-separated, one I4.below-contrast-floor accent-vs-surface) and one known-bad; on the advisory reconstructed-gradient matrix 11 more (5 endorsements, 5 acceptable, 1 known-bad), all accent-vs-ramp. decisions.decision: WHERE A CONVERSATIONAL RULING AND A RECORDED ROUND ANSWER CONFLICT, THE CHAT IS CANONICAL. The round is an instrument for eliciting the reviewer's judgement; when the reviewer states the judgement directly, the instrument's reading of it is not a second opinion. THREE CASES ON ONE DAY ESTABLISHED THIS: (1) the toolbox adjudication was settled in chat while its 42-item round sat pushed and unanswered; (2) endorsement-recheck-1 was overridden in chat after being answered - 'ignore my review of endorsement-recheck, the rule is right in both cases'; (3) dropped-colors-1 was stopped mid-round and settled in chat. THE CONFLICTING ANSWERS ARE ANNOTATED, NEVER DELETED AND NEVER RETRACTED. A dated `note` record is filed against the affected item saying what superseded it and why; the answer stays in the log, resolves normally, and keeps counting wherever it counted. An agent retracting a reviewer's answer is a move nobody has authorised. AND THE ROUND STILL HAS TO BE EXPLAINED. In all three cases the chat did not merely outrank the round - it revealed something wrong with it: an unanswered round asked 42 questions the reviewer preferred to answer in one pass, an answered item had been served without the explanation it needed, and a third round was built on a measurement the reviewer rejected outright. decisions.decision: THE REVIEWER'S TWO ACCENT POSITIONS OF 2026-08-04 ARE NOT A CONTRADICTION - THEY ARE A STIMULUS-REALISM EFFECT. On the same day: in accent-functional-1, isoluminant accents at distances around 0.06-0.09 on synthetic panels were called WORKING accents, 28 of 31 stimuli carrying exactly zero luminance contrast; and on a real cover, an accent at OKLab distance 0.121 - roughly TWICE the distance of the synthetic ones - was called UNREADABLE. THE DIAGNOSIS IS THE STIMULUS, NOT THE WORDING AND NOT THE CRITERION. Synthetic flat-field panels flatter isoluminant accents: a uniform field gives the eye an uninterrupted edge and no competing structure, so a colour difference that survives there is doing far less work than the same difference on real artwork. Real artwork surfaces have texture, gradient, noise and neighbouring colour, and they eat exactly this kind of contrast. The round did not measure a threshold that was too low; it measured a threshold ON THE WRONG SURFACE. CONSEQUENCES, ALL THREE: (1) accent-functional-1's refusal STANDS, with this diagnosis attached - see d-2026-08-04-accent-functional-round-1-refuses-its-own-fit-and-excludes-the-placeholder. It was a clean round and its fit is still correctly refused. (3) ACCENT_FUNCTIONAL_DISTANCE STAYS 0.14591 AND STAYS [UNCALIBRATED] MEANWHILE. AND THE TWO BODIES OF EVIDENCE POINT IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS, WHICH IS THE HONEST STATE. The synthetic round excluded the placeholder at 95% from BELOW - its evidence says the number should come DOWN. The real-cover judgement says an accent at 0.121 is unreadable, so the number should go UP, toward the placeholder or past it. GENUINELY UNRESOLVED UNTIL THE REAL-STIMULUS ROUND RUNS. decisions.decision: SAM AT RUNTIME IS DOWNGRADED FROM A LIVE OPTION TO A THING NOBODY IS EXPECTED TO WANT - AND IT IS NOT BANNED. Reviewer, 2026-08-04, verbatim, emphasis the reviewer's own: "TBH it's even better if we don't need SAM at runtime, let it just be a dev tool to help with iteration autonomy. I'm *open* to having it at runtime if any agent has a brilliant idea of how it would improve accuracy, but it's not a requirement". READ THE EMPHASIS ON *open*: IT IS LOAD-BEARING AND IT IS WHY THIS IS NOT A PROHIBITION. What moved is the EXPECTATION, not the rule. Before this, a design that wanted SAM at runtime faced four conjunctive conditions and had to argue them; after this it faces the same four conditions AND the standing fact that the reviewer would rather not need it at all. WHAT DID NOT MOVE: the four conditions of PHASE_0_DECISIONS.md 6.1 are UNCHANGED AND STILL BIND ANYTHING THAT WANTS SAM AT RUNTIME - (1) no upstream model feeds it; (2) provably deterministic, MEASURED AND SATISFIED for the pinned stack (sam-determinism-1); (3) fast enough, NOT SATISFIED - the reviewer ruled the measured cost "counts as slow" and requires "very good reasons", and the number a proposal must quote is the ~6.2 s COLD per-call figure, not the 2.7-4.3 s warm band; (4) plain-code methods exhausted, or SAM demonstrably more reliable than them. THE DOOR THIS RULING LEAVES OPEN IS NARROW AND NAMED: "a brilliant idea of how it would improve accuracy". AN ACCURACY ARGUMENT IS THE ADMISSIBLE KIND. Convenience, developer speed, familiarity, 'it was the obvious tool' and silence are not, and none of them was admissible before either - what is new is that the reviewer has now said in their own words which kind of argument they would listen to. AND THE DEV-TIME USE IS ENDORSED BY NAME, NOT MERELY TOLERATED: "let it just be a dev tool to help with iteration autonomy" is the reviewer positively wanting the oracle's SAM masks spent on iteration autonomy, which is what the oracle was built for and what V3_PLAN.md 5 already says it is for.

It is **never a runtime component**." AND ITS FIRST BULLET, WHICH IS 4's SENTENCE RESTATED WITH ITS SCOPE VISIBLE: "**Makes scene-parse-first evaluable** - intermediate representations scored directly, not just final palettes."
